examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Counting sort takes Θ(n+k) for range k. LSD radix sorting requires a stable digit sort so later passes preserve earlier digit ordering. Choose digit width by balancing pass count with per-pass alphabet size. Key width is part of the assumptions, not always a hidden constant.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
How many base-16 LSD radix passes are needed for unsigned 20-bit keys?

**Answer: 5.** A hexadecimal digit contains four bits. Required passes=ceil(20/4)=5. Leading zero digits can be included without changing the final order.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Signed keys require a sign-handling convention. An unstable per-digit sort can invalidate LSD radix sorting.

Counting sort is not efficient when the key range is enormous compared with n.
